From: Alex Turner <alex@zenova.ai>

Cc: procurement@zenova.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:43 -0700
Subject: Zenova embed requirements + baseline pricing request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers you showed look promising for our semantic search use case. Procurement asked me to gather firm baseline pricing so they can run internal modeling. A few concrete items we need: 

- Baseline hosted embeddings price(s): do you price per-vector or per-token (or both)? Please give the unit price for the common vector dimensions (256, 512, 768) and the mapping rules if you use token-equivalents.
- Which Redwood embedding models are supported under the hosted API and which are in the "recommended for production" tier? Any dimension limits we should know about?
- Are there packaging options (monthly vector bundles, committed QPS tiers) and how do discounts step with committed volumes?
- Any differences for EU-hosted models/regions we should account for (pricing or compliance add-ons)?

We're planning an initial pilot (~5M vectors/month, 512-dim) and a potential ramp to ~120M vectors/month over 12 months if the latency/cost profile is acceptable. Procurement would also like a sample quote and a list of required contract/legal items.

I've attached the RFP summary for context (Zenova_RFP_2026_Q3.pdf). Can you confirm whether you have a standard embedding ratecard we can use for budgeting?

Thanks — if it's easier to hop on a 30-min call we can do that as well.

—Alex
Director, Search & Data Platforms
Zenova AI

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:05:17 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zenova embed requirements + baseline pricing request

Hi Alex — great to hear from you and thanks for the RFP. Looping in Aditya (our commercial lead) and Marissa (solutions/legal touchpoint) who will help with the quote and contract items.

Quick answers and a baseline to get you started:

Baseline hosted embeddings (public ratecard summary):
- Per-vector pricing model (primary):
  - 256-dim: $0.0000025 per vector
  - 512-dim: $0.0000040 per vector
  - 768-dim: $0.0000065 per vector
- Per-token mapping: we optionally report a token-equivalent for accounting, but billing is by vector by default. Token-equivalent = ceil(dimensions / 64) * 10 tokens (used only for reports).

Supported models (hosted): redwood-embed-small (256d), redwood-embed-medium (512d), redwood-embed-large (768d) — all are GA and in our recommended production tier. We also support custom quantized variants for private deployments; for hosted we expose the three sizes above. Max dimension on hosted is 1024; beyond that we recommend private deployment.

Packaging / discounts:
- Monthly bundles: 1M, 5M, 25M, 100M vector pre-purchase SKUs.
- Volume discounts (committed monthly vector volumes, applied as percent off baseline price):
  - 5M monthly commit: 10% off
  - 25M monthly commit: 18% off
  - 100M monthly commit: 28% off
- Ramp credits: for customers moving from pilot -> committed we offer a one-time ramp credit equal to 5% of first quarter spend.

EU region: same baseline list prices but +5% region surcharge for EU-hosted inference (covers data residency and additional compliance controls).

I've attached our canonical ratecard spreadsheet (RDW_EMBED_RATECARD_2026.xlsx) and a quick acknowledgement PDF (Zenova_RFP_ack.pdf).

Next steps: could you confirm the expected committed vector volume and whether you need EU-hosted inference? If the 120M vector ramp looks realistic we can run a tailored commercial that includes staged discounts and a service SLA. Aditya — can you prepare a starter quote once Alex confirms the volume and region? Marissa — flag any required redlines to the standard SOW.

Happy to do a 30-min call — I have availability Thu 16th 10–11am PT.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the details and for confirming the pilot dates. A few commercial clarifications from our side: 

- Prepay / bundle behavior: if you prepay at contract signature for a 100M bundle (single-year commitment) we can apply the 28% bundle discount from month 1 for the prepaid amount. For a staged ramp we typically do a blended schedule (e.g., prepay 50M at signature at the 100M bundle price point, remaining monthly usage billed at actual usage with the committed discounts applied if you hit them).
- For the 120M target we can offer a promotional incentive: 25% off baseline (instead of 28%) + first-quarter ramp credit waived to simplify invoicing, provided you sign a 12-month committed purchase with a 60% prepay. This is negotiable but gives procurement a concrete option to model.
- Data retention / KV cache: Redwood keeps ephemeral KV cache entries for up to 72 hours by default for latency optimizations; we can increase or disable caching per contract for compliance (there may be a <small>performance vs cost</small> trade-off). We'll surface the SOC2 artifact package to your security team during the procurement review.

Marissa — please prep a draft SOW and mark any standard security addenda we should include for EU data residency. Alex — I'll issue a starter pro-forma and an example invoice template after the call; expect a draft in 48 hours.

Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
